exp-34: reduce hard_neg_weight 1.0→0.5; CLS pooling; std InfoNCE; top_k=7; test if in-batch negatives dominate further helps; new champion exp-33 primary=55.16

exp-44: latent_attn pooling (K=4 trainable queries cross-attend encoder output, NV-Embed-v2 style); 5-min exploration; hard_neg_weight=1.0; baseline exp-33 primary=55.16
exp-45: CLS pooling quick baseline (2+3+2 min); hard_neg_weight=1.0; to compare vs exp-44 latent_attn same training duration; baseline exp-33 primary=55.16
exp-46: latent_attn pooling full run (15+45+45 min); K=4 trainable query vectors cross-attend encoder output; hard_neg_weight=1.0; NV-Embed-v2 style; baseline exp-33 primary=55.16

exp-48: add HotpotQA retrieval pairs (question→supporting passage); full run 15+45+5+45 min; CLS pooling; target retrieval (SciFact 44.5, NFCorpus 19.19); baseline exp-33 primary=55.16
exp-49: HotpotQA data + short fine-tuning (5 min); fix exp-48 overfitting (45min FT on 8000 samples = 58 epochs hurt); contrastive 45min; FT 5min; baseline exp-33 primary=55.16
exp-50: ablation remove HotpotQA, keep 5-min FT; isolate whether improvement in exp-49 (55.76) came from HotpotQA data vs short FT; baseline exp-33 primary=55.16 (no HotpotQA, 5-min FT same)
exp-51: extend contrastive to 60min (was 45min); HotpotQA included; 5-min FT; hypothesis: model not fully converging at 45min; baseline exp-49 primary=55.76
exp-52: extend contrastive to 90min (was 60min); HotpotQA included; 5-min FT; hypothesis: more training = better; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-53: add TriviaQA retrieval pairs (question→answer+context); 60-min contrastive; HotpotQA included; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-54: larger contrastive batch_size=128 (was 64); more in-batch negatives per InfoNCE step; 60-min contrastive; HotpotQA; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-55: lower temperature 0.04 (was 0.05) for contrastive+FT; 60-min contrastive; batch=64; HotpotQA; hypothesis: harder discrimination = better embeddings; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-56: add PAWS paraphrase pairs (adversarial) to fix SICK-R regression from HotpotQA; 60-min contrastive; temp=0.05; batch=64; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-57: symmetric InfoNCE (bidirectional query→pos + pos→query); 60-min contrastive; HotpotQA; hypothesis: 2x training signal improves representations; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81

exp-58: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) - InfoNCE at dims [768,512,256,128,64] averaged; 60-min contrastive; HotpotQA; hypothesis: MRL forces better info packing in early dims; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-59: extend warmup to 20min (was 15min); 60-min contrastive; HotpotQA; hypothesis: more paraphrase warmup fixes SICK-R regression; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-60: implement actual cosine LR decay (was broken - lr_schedule config had no effect); warmup+cosine_decay now applied to contrastive; 60-min contrastive; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-61: fix crash from exp-60; actual cosine LR decay working; warmup uses linear_warmup_constant; contrastive uses cosine_decay from 5e-5 to 0; 60-min; HotpotQA; baseline exp-51 primary=56.81
exp-62: higher contrastive LR 8e-5 (was 5e-5) with cosine decay; 60-min; HotpotQA; hypothesis: higher peak LR + cosine decay = better convergence; baseline exp-61 primary=57.11
exp-63: lower contrastive LR 3e-5 (was 5e-5) with cosine decay; 60-min; HotpotQA; hypothesis: gentler learning keeps STS quality; baseline exp-61 primary=57.11
exp-64: warmup uses cosine_decay LR=1.5e-4 (was linear_warmup_constant LR=1e-4); contrastive cosine_decay 5e-5; 60-min; HotpotQA; baseline exp-61 primary=57.11
exp-65: instruction-tuning for embeddings - task-specific query prefixes (e.g. 'Retrieve a passage that answers:'); 60-min cosine_decay contrastive; HotpotQA; baseline exp-61 primary=57.11
exp-66: contrastive 75min (interpolate between 60 and 90); cosine_decay LR=5e-5; HotpotQA; hypothesis: 60<75<90 sweet spot; baseline exp-61 primary=57.11 (60min) vs exp-52 56.45 (90min)
exp-67: time-based cosine LR decay (fix: was step-estimate based which under-counted for long runs); 60-min contrastive; baseline exp-61 primary=57.11 (was step-based)
exp-68: 75-min contrastive with time-based cosine decay (exp-66 used buggy step-based); baseline exp-67 primary=57.51 (60-min)
exp-69: expand hard neg mining 8K→16K + fine-tuning 5min→10min; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51
exp-70: activate hard neg loss in fine-tuning (weight=2.0 vs 1.0 which was disabled); hypothesis: explicit hard negs boost retrieval; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-74: fix NaN gradient bug (attention mask -inf→-1e9 prevents all-masked softmax rows) + max_seq_length=512 (was 256 for all prior exps) + data scaling 50K/dataset (~328K pairs); batch=64 no grad_accum; hypothesis: longer sequences improve retrieval tasks; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-75: mean pooling (was CLS for all prior exps); all other params match exp-67 baseline; hypothesis: mean pooling captures richer all-token representation vs single CLS token, expected to improve retrieval and clustering; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51 (CLS pooling)

exp-71: disable source_stratification (mixed batches instead of single-source); killed manually — NaN loss from first step, root cause was -inf attention masks not stratification; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-72: data scaling 30K→50K/dataset + grad accum fix; NaN loss — root cause was -inf in attention masks (misattributed to LLRD/EMA/grad_ckpt); multiple attempts, all NaN; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51
exp-73: max_seq_length=512 + batch=32 + grad_accum=2; NaN loss — same -inf attention mask root cause; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51
exp-76: disable fine-tuning stage (duration=0) + extend contrastive to 65min; eval hung during clustering task (fixed in c55dcaf); scores from run.log; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-77: SimCLR projection head (2-layer MLP 768→768→768 with GELU, train on projected space, eval on raw encoder); all other params match exp-67 baseline; hypothesis: projection head absorbs task noise → cleaner encoder representations → better generalization across all task types; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-78: data scaling 50K/dataset (was 30K in exp-67 baseline, ~328K→~500K pairs); also fix: cache key now includes max_rows (previously stale 30K cache was reused); all other params match exp-67; hypothesis: more diverse training signal improves generalization; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-79: reproduce exp-67 baseline — revert attention masking to padding-only (no sliding window), restore grad_accum=4+batch=32 for FT; hypothesis: sliding window mask introduced in exp-73 caused regression in subsequent experiments; expected: ~57.5 (match exp-67); baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-80: LLRD decay=0.95 (lower layers get smaller LR, standard BERT FT technique) + increase MTEB timeout to 10min (fix RedditClustering timeout); grad_accum=4, batch=64/32, CLS pooling, seq_len=256; hypothesis: LLRD preserves pretrained lower-layer features while adapting upper layers → +1-2 points; baseline exp-67 primary=57.51

exp-81: fix critical bug — grad_accum=1 (exp-67 config said 4 but code had NO grad_accum implementation, so actual was 1; exps 78-80 accidentally used grad_accum=4 causing 4x larger effective batch and fewer optimizer steps); LLRD=0.95; MTEB timeout=10min; hypothesis: fixing grad_accum to match exp-67's actual behavior + LLRD should reproduce/beat 57.51

exp-82: exact exp-67 code reproduction (reverted train.py + model.py to exp-67 commit d9d0497); only diff is config fields (llrd_decay, ema_decay, etc.) which are ignored by old code; hypothesis: should reproduce ~57.51 primary score

exp-83: data scaling 100K/dataset (was 30K in exp-82 baseline); expect ~500K+ pairs from larger datasets (reddit, NQ, MS-MARCO); all other code identical to exp-82; hypothesis: more diverse training data is highest-ROI improvement per program.md; baseline exp-82 primary=57.72

exp-85: symmetric InfoNCE loss (bidirectional: query→positive + positive→query) for both warmup and contrastive stages; 90-min contrastive; hypothesis: symmetric loss doubles contrastive signal and improves retrieval tasks; baseline exp-84 primary=57.89
exp-84: extend contrastive to 90min; INCOMPLETE eval — 7/8 tasks (RedditClustering timed out, scored as 0); NOT comparable to full 8-task evals
exp-87: baseline rerun with L2 grad norm (REGRESSED — reverted); full 8/8 eval; L2 clip cost 48% steps; baseline exp-82 primary=57.72

exp-88: MinHash cross-dataset deduplication (word 3-gram, 64 perms, threshold=0.5); removes near-duplicate pairs across 10 training datasets; hypothesis: dedup removes noisy/redundant pairs that waste compute and bias contrastive loss (false negatives); all other config identical to exp-82 baseline (60-min contrastive, temp=0.05, CLS, seq_len=256, batch=64); baseline exp-82 primary=57.72

exp-89: fix hard neg gate (>0.0 not >1.0) + enable hard negs in fine-tuning (weight=1.0, natural scale); fix hard neg loss formula (remove logit amplification that destroyed exp-70); hypothesis: hard neg mining was always wasted because the gate silently disabled hard negs in fine-tuning — enabling them at natural scale should improve retrieval tasks; baseline exp-82 primary=57.72

exp-91: data scaling 100K/dataset (655K pairs) + 120min contrastive (2x baseline); fix max_rows_per_dataset to read from config (was hardcoded 30K); exp-83 used 100K data but only 60min training — model saw each pair ~1.5x vs 3x at baseline; hypothesis: proportional training time with more data will improve score; baseline exp-82 primary=57.72

exp-92: LLRD decay=0.95 (layer-wise LR decay); lower layers get 34%-57% of base LR, preserving pretrained features while adapting upper layers more; standard for BERT fine-tuning (GTE, NV-Embed, Arctic-Embed all use this); all other config same as exp-91 (100K/dataset, 120min contrastive); baseline exp-91 primary=57.91

exp-93: 2x contrastive LR (1e-4 vs 5e-5); with 655K pairs and 120min, higher LR may push further into the loss landscape; warmup LR unchanged at 1e-4; hypothesis: higher LR exploits the larger dataset more effectively; all other config same as exp-91 (100K/dataset, 120min, CLS, temp=0.05, batch=64); baseline exp-91 primary=57.91

exp-94: batch=128 contrastive (2x in-batch negatives, 127 vs 63); linear-scaled LR=1e-4 (from batch=64/LR=5e-5); exp-93 showed LR=1e-4 at batch=64 regressed (56.60 vs 57.91) — the proper test requires batch=128 per linear scaling rule; more negatives per step improves contrastive signal, especially for retrieval; all other config same as exp-91; baseline exp-91 primary=57.91

exp-94: batch=96 contrastive (1.5x in-batch negatives, 95 vs 63); linear-scaled LR=7.5e-5 (from batch=64/LR=5e-5); batch=128 hung at 51GB due to Metal memory; batch=96 stays under tiled-loss threshold, uses standard InfoNCE; more negatives per step improves contrastive signal for retrieval; all other config same as exp-91; baseline exp-91 primary=57.91

exp-95: add PubMedQA biomedical training data (211K question-context pairs from qiaojin/PubMedQA pqa_artificial); directly targets our weakest tasks: NFCorpus=20.31, SciFact=49.52; no other config changes from exp-91 baseline (batch=64, LR=5e-5, 120min contrastive, CLS, temp=0.05); hypothesis: biomedical domain data improves retrieval scores; baseline exp-91 primary=57.91

exp-96: PubMedQA + 140min contrastive (proportional to 756K pairs); exp-95 showed PubMedQA helped SciFact (+2.47) and clustering (+2.65 20news) but STS regressed (-2.18) — likely from insufficient training with 15% more data; 140min gives same pairs-per-minute as exp-91 (120min/655K); all other config same as exp-91; baseline exp-91 primary=57.91, exp-95 primary=57.71

exp-97: extended contrastive to 180min (exp-96 loss 0.312 not saturated); PubMedQA data (756K pairs); same LR=5e-5, batch=64, CLS, temp=0.05; 180min gives ~4.5 passes over 756K pairs vs 3.5 in exp-96; hypothesis: more training improves all task categories; baseline exp-96 primary=58.23 (NEW BEST)

exp-98: add S2ORC scientific title-abstract pairs (sentence-transformers/s2orc, streaming); targets weak retrieval (SciFact, NFCorpus) and clustering diversity; 140min contrastive (180min overfit in exp-97); code adds s2orc_title_abstract format handler; hypothesis: scientific domain data improves retrieval like PubMedQA did; baseline exp-96 primary=58.23
